papers.title: Electron Spin Decoherence due to Hindered Rotation in Donor-Bridge-Acceptor Linked Molecules
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.summary: Molecular-dynamics-assisted spin simulations connect hindered rotation to exchange fluctuations and radical-pair dephasing. A reduced Liouville model reproduces the more expensive simulations in the tested regimes when its parameters are estimated appropriately.
papers.whyRelevant: Directly relevant to separating conformational motion from intrinsic spin-decoherence mechanisms in molecular radicals.

relatedPapers.reason: Both focus on organic radical spin systems and limitations to their quantum behavior.

papers.title: Effect of Chirality on Carrier Spin Relaxation Dynamics in CsPbBr3 Perovskite Quantum Dots
papers.authors: Mariam Khvichia, Celia Todd, Edmund Siu, Yuan Ping, Jin Z. Zhang
papers.summary: Spin-selective transient absorption compares chiral perovskite quantum dots over temperature. The measured spin relaxation changes little with cooling, motivating an interpretation in which chirality changes the dominant relaxation mechanism.
papers.whyRelevant: An adjacent-material comparison for testing how chirality and phonons jointly influence spin relaxation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate chirality and lattice coupling in spin dynamics.

papers.title: Understanding the effects of competing spin-pair dephasing pathways in molecular spins
papers.authors: Timothy J Krogmeier, James Bradley, Anthony W Schlimgen, Kade Head-Marsden
papers.summary: A non-Markovian molecular-spin model resolves dephasing contributions from nuclear-spin pairs within a molecule, within its solvent and across their boundary. The analysis suggests a workflow for identifying which chemical changes could improve coherence.
papers.whyRelevant: A close reference for choosing ligand and solvent modifications based on the dominant spin-bath pathway.

relatedPapers.reason: Both target longer coherence in molecular spin systems.

papers.title: Winding holonomy and modular noise spectroscopy in discrete time crystals
papers.summary: A theoretical Floquet framework relates drive winding, phase tracking and pulse-area errors to discrete-time-crystal responses. Simulations distinguish signatures of controller phase slips, phase diffusion and systematic timing offsets.
papers.whyRelevant: Offers a specialized noise-diagnosis perspective for driven spin systems, rather than a ready-made molecular-qubit protocol.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine control errors in periodically driven quantum dynamics.

papers.title: Action-detected two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy: Theory, methods, and future directions
papers.authors: Luca Bolzonello, Matteo Bruschi, Edoardo Amarotti, Zachary Faitz, Julian Lüttig, Joseph Wragg, Stefan Müller, Xiaoji Xu, Andreas Jakobsson, Pavel Malý, Barbara Fresch, Elisabetta Collini, Donatas Zigmantas, Tönu Pullerits, Tobias Brixner, Jennifer P. Ogilvie, Martin Zanni, Niek F. van Hulst
papers.summary: This methods review explains action-detected two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy using fluorescence, photocurrent or related observables. It contrasts experimental flexibility with interpretation challenges from incoherent mixing and detection nonlinearities.
papers.whyRelevant: Useful supporting methodology for reading molecular excited-state experiments and avoiding detection-induced artifacts.

relatedPapers.reason: Both emphasize separating genuine physical response from measurement artifacts.

papers.title: Quantum sensing in the presence of pulse errors and qubit leakage
papers.authors: David M. Lancaster, Muhammad Ali Shahbaz, Hamed Goli Yousefabad, Sanway Chatterjee, Eegan Ram, Jonathan D. Weinstein
papers.summary: Simulations and experiments compare dynamical-decoupling sequences under rotation errors, detuning and leakage. Their sensing performance can differ substantially even when coherence-time measurements alone suggest a different comparison.
papers.whyRelevant: A close match to the group's control work: a sequence that preserves coherence need not preserve sensing accuracy.

relatedPapers.reason: Both evaluate and mitigate control errors in dynamical decoupling.

papers.title: High-Field Spin Dynamics of Photoexcited Pentacene at 9.2 T by Time-Resolved Pulsed EPR and Vector DC Magnetic-Field Sensing
papers.authors: Duhan Zhang, Zeyu Wang, Johan van Tol, Yifan Quan
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: Optically synchronized high-frequency pulsed EPR resolves pentacene triplet populations, relaxation and coherence at high magnetic field. A sensing protocol combines inequivalent molecular sites and orientation-dependent decay to infer a DC field's magnitude and direction.
papers.whyRelevant: A close methodological match for molecular-spin sensing and the interpretation of photoexcited triplet dynamics.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use molecular spin dynamics as a sensing resource.

papers.title: Laser-enhanced quantum sensing boosts sensitivity and dynamic range
papers.authors: Florian Schall, Lukas Lindner, Yves Rottstaedt, Marcel Rattunde, Florentin Reiter, Rüdiger Quay, Roman Bek, Alexander M. Zaitsev, Takeshi Ohshima, Andrew D. Greentree, Jan Jeske
papers.summary: NV centers integrated into a laser cavity modulate the lasing threshold through magnetic resonance. The experiment demonstrates large optical contrast and analyzes a photon-shot-noise sensitivity bound while retaining a broad dynamic range.
papers.whyRelevant: A readout-engineering comparison; the calculated sensitivity bound should be distinguished from achieved experimental sensitivity.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate measurement strategies that improve quantum-sensor readout.

papers.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
papers.authors: E. Mayner, Y. Zhumagulov, C. de Giorgio, F. Chu, P. P. Swain, G. E. Fantner, A. Kis, O. V. Yazyev, A. Radenovic
papers.summary: A PbI2–hBN heterostructure increases boron-vacancy emission through interlayer optical coupling while retaining ODMR contrast. Measurements and calculations link the enhancement to energy transfer and a photon-ratchet mechanism.
papers.whyRelevant: Shows how a material interface can improve a weak spin-defect signal without requiring strong electronic hybridization.

relatedPapers.reason: Both link optical access to localized spins with the surrounding material environment.

papers.title: Quantum Ghost Spectroscopy Reveals Hidden Coherence in Molecular Aggregates
papers.authors: Mingran Zhang, Yihe Xu, Vladislav V. Yakovlev, Zhedong Zhang
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: A simulated quantum-ghost spectroscopy protocol uses entangled light to isolate excited-state emission in molecular aggregates. Vibronic simulations reveal electronic and vibrational coherence pathways that are obscured in conventional signals.
papers.whyRelevant: An adjacent optical approach to separating coupled molecular dynamics; the evidence is theoretical rather than an experimental sensing demonstration.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address the coupling of molecular electronic or spin degrees of freedom to vibrations.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage for Sensing Properties of Classical Fields
papers.authors: Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, Ishaan Kannan
papers.summary: A quantum signal-learning framework uses two-mode squeezing and homodyne measurements to estimate multiple properties of classical fields. The analysis identifies sensing tasks where correlations improve sample efficiency over specified classical baselines.
papers.whyRelevant: Broadens the comparison between single-parameter sensitivity and learning several properties from the same measurement record.

relatedPapers.reason: Both focus on extracting useful field information through measurement design.

papers.title: Interface-Engineered Flexible Conductive Metal–Organic Framework Films for Multimodal Energy Applications
papers.authors: Shengyang Zhou, Zhixiang Dai, Jingyu Cao, Chao Xu
papers.summary: This Account reviews interfacial growth and processing of conductive MOF films, including assemblies on cellulose nanofibers. It connects morphology, pore networks and interfacial chemistry with mixed transport and flexible device integration.
papers.whyRelevant: A processing overview relevant to preserving conductivity when moving from crystals to usable film architectures.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect material morphology with electronic-device fabrication.

papers.title: Spin Seebeck Effect Induced by Quantum Interference in Organic Collinear Antiferromagnetic Molecular Junctions
papers.authors: Han Ma, Hui-Qing Zhang, Xiao-Bei Zhang, Guang-Ping Zhang, Jun-Feng Ren, Gui-Chao Hu
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: Model and first-principles calculations predict spin thermoelectric response in an organic antiferromagnetic molecular junction. Spin-dependent destructive interference, rather than ordinary energy-level spin splitting, produces the proposed effect.
papers.whyRelevant: A useful reminder that connectivity and interference can generate spin-selective transport without ferromagnetic electrodes.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern emergent electronic and magnetic behavior in molecular materials.

papers.title: Signatures of Band-like Charge Carrier Transport in a Three-Dimensional Fe-HHTP Metal–Organic Framework
papers.authors: Md Soif Ahmed, Marina I. Schönherr, Marco Ballabio, Sandra M. Estévez, Mariela Menghini, Dana D. Medina, Enrique Cánovas
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: DC transport and terahertz spectroscopy examine a three-dimensional Fe-HHTP framework. Their combined analysis supports mobile carriers with backscattering and thermally activated density, reconciling band-like local dynamics with activated macroscopic conductivity.
papers.whyRelevant: A particularly useful example of combining frequency- and temperature-dependent measurements to distinguish transport mechanisms.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate how to interpret measured conductivity in MOFs.

papers.title: Subverting the Dominant Paradigm in Metal–Organic Framework Activation
papers.authors: Evelyn C. Peterson, George W. Fritze, Nicholas A. Tomalia, Adam J. Matzger
papers.summary: Experiments test direct thermal activation of several MOFs without the usual solvent-exchange sequence. Thermal analysis and NMR show that solvent removal competes with linker decomposition and that residual solvents influence collapse.
papers.whyRelevant: Directly useful for selecting activation conditions before measuring intrinsic properties of framework samples.

relatedPapers.reason: Both require separating sample treatment effects from intrinsic framework behavior.

papers.title: Precise molecular sieving in polycrystalline covalent organic framework membranes
papers.authors: Xiansong Shi, Haipei Shao, Xin Zhang, Fen Huang, Qixing Liu, He Li, Wei Zhao, Junyu Ren, Yunchuan Pu, Wen-Hua Li, Nengxiu Zhu, Ming Lin, Dan Zhao
papers.summary: A monomer-driven route forms intergrown COF crystals into thin membranes under ambient conditions. Structural and transport measurements connect long-range crystallographic order with molecular selectivity and mechanical properties.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant to controlling crystallinity and intergrowth instead of relying on nominal pore size alone.

relatedPapers.reason: Both link synthetic control to framework crystallinity.

papers.title: Single Crystals of a Two‐Dimensional Interpenetrated Covalent Organic Framework for Stabilizing Lithium Metal Anodes
papers.authors: Jinghang Wu, Yuchan Zhang, Lei Zhang, Qianfeng Gu, Xin Wang, Zihao Chen, Tuoya Naren, Xiang Wang, Qichun Zhang
papers.summary: Single-crystal diffraction resolves an unusual interpenetrated two-dimensional boron–nitrogen framework with interdigitated neighboring layers. The reinforced architecture combines structural stability with ion-interacting sites for a demonstrated electrode coating.
papers.whyRelevant: The main relevance is the resolved interpenetration and stacking architecture, rather than the battery application.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect layer organization with the properties of extended frameworks.

papers.title: Bridging Marcus–Landauer Transport Regimes in Orbital-Gated Molecular Junctions
papers.authors: Minwoo Song, Jongwoo Nam, Hyemin Lee, Changjun Lee, Donguk Kim, Ryong-Gyu Lee, Minsu Jeong, Yong-Hoon Kim, Keehoon Kang, Takhee Lee
papers.summary: Gate-tunable molecular transistors cross between thermally activated hopping and approximately temperature-independent tunneling. Experiments on redox-active monolayers and accompanying theory connect the transition with the alignment of molecular orbitals and electrode electrochemical potentials.
papers.whyRelevant: Directly relevant to identifying transport mechanisms and interpreting contacts in molecular and framework devices.

relatedPapers.reason: Directly relevant to identifying transport mechanisms and interpreting contacts in molecular and framework devices.

papers.title: Tuning the Raman/Orbach Relaxation Ratio in Co2IIIDyIII Single-Molecule Magnets through Acetate-to-Nitrate Substitution
papers.authors: Fan-Fan Chen, Yang Zhou, Chuang Hu, Zhao-Bo Hu, Hui-Sheng Wang
papers.summary: Replacing an acetate ligand with nitrate changes the balance of Raman and Orbach relaxation in dysprosium-containing molecular magnets. Magnetic measurements and electronic-structure calculations connect this change with the coordination environment and magnetic-axis orientation.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant to chemical control of spin–lattice relaxation; slow magnetic relaxation alone does not demonstrate coherent qubit operation.

relatedPapers.reason: Relevant to chemical control of spin–lattice relaxation; slow magnetic relaxation alone does not demonstrate coherent qubit operation.
